convention: literal line-by-line, rules 1-7 of batch H03's brief
reasoning_summary:
1.17.9 haediliae is doubtful (kids vs a place-name); taken as nom. pl. 'kids', noted.
1.18.1 severis read as perf. subj. of sero 'plant', not severus; prius + abl. vite = in preference to the vine.
1.20.10 tu bibes kept over the variant tum bibes; mea ... pocula spans lines 10-12, kept split.
1.23.5-7 transmitted veris inhorruit / adventus foliis kept against the emendation vepris ... ad ventum; noted.
1.25.11-12 inter-/lunia split across the line break as in the Latin; moechos rendered plainly as 'adulterers'; dry leaves / Eurus metaphor kept literal and glossed.
1.27 metaphors (wound, arrow, Charybdis, Chimaera) kept literal with notes; tmesis quae te cumque noted.
1.28 long hyperbata (morituro tibi, fraudem nocituram, vagae harenae particulam) kept on their own lines with agreement notes; source milestone says Alcaic but the ode is Alcmanian couplets (flagged in note on 1.28.1).
Throughout, hyperbaton left in place so each English line carries only its Latin line's words; 'non sine' and 'nec ... nihil' kept unresolved; supplied possessives noted.
